title: Short ciphered biglietto (c. 13r) in the Medici letters of Ginori Conti 29.137, cc. 1-39
correspondents: Medici circle (Lorenzo de' Medici / Niccolo Michelozzi correspondence of 1481)
shelfmark: Florence, Biblioteca nazionale centrale, Ginori Conti 29.137 (cc. 1-39) (Manus CNMD record 611145)
status: Existing (edition), probable (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026): the 1964 Censimento of Lorenzo's letters lists two Lorenzo to Michelozzi pieces in GC 29.137 (July? and 5 Aug 1481), so Lettere VI (1481-82) very likely prints this biglietto. Not checked in the volume. Earlier note: Manus: 'Il biglietto e in scrittura cifrata.' Sender, addressee and date of the biglietto not given. Not on DECODE. Manus gives the sheet-by-sheet description; the 29.114.a key sheets (Otto di Pratica, Dieci di Balia) are on the same fund and may fit. | Vetting 5 Nov 2026: leaf seen on the BNCF viewer (40x209 mm strip, four lines of symbol cipher, no gloss); held back from the catalogue until Lorenzo de Medici, Lettere VI (1481-82) is checked for a printed decipherment.
why: A short Medici cipher note of 1481 (Pazzi-war aftermath); cheap to test against the Florentine keys.

vetting_note: Edition question settled, contemporary-clear question not. Censimento (1964, Google Books seEYGFQqM1kC, old interface in Chrome) p. 48: its two Lorenzo pieces in 'BNF, GC, 137' are '[Niccolò Michelozzi] [3 lug. 1481?]' and '[Niccolò Michelozzi] 5 ago. 1481' (snippet images read); the Censimento gives no folios for GC 137, and Lettere V p. 262 (archive.org bwb_KU-999-230_5, search 'GC, 137') identifies the first as cc. 20r-21v, Lettere VI no. 509 p. 26 (bwb_KU-999-229_6) the second as cc. 6r-9r. The '137, c. 13' phrase hit on p. 48 could not be placed in any snippet and is not one of these entries; Lettere VI has no hit for Palavisino, Strasoldano or ghibellino. So no edition prints c. 13. Alignment test of c. 13r (BNCF0003827895, 985x217) against the clear strip c. 12r (BNCF0003827893, 1036x576, transcribed: 'El conte Girolamo ha sollecitato l'andata di m. Ascanio a Roma, qual si stima sia opera del S. L[odovi]co ... el palavisino ... m. Johanfrancesco ... el S. Lco et m. palavisino et strasoldano è sospecto assai parendo loro che lui sia di ghibellini', 261 letters): c. 13r transcribed to 263 tokens over 37 sign types (scratchpad c32/tools/align.py). Results: (1) the sign '11' occurs at least 8 times, so it is not the 'll' of sollecitato/ghibellini; (2) the near-repeat ('5 g 5 3 n m π 11 b t' end of line 1 / '5 y 5 3 n π b t' mid line 3) sits at about 22% and 61% of the strip, not where the two 'palavisino' fall in the clear (49%, 74%); it would fit 'el S. Lco et' (27%, 70%) better, but no consistent sign-to-letter table was found for it together with 'sollecitato'; (3) a beam-search crib alignment scored the c. 12r text no better than three unrelated Italian controls (cost 451 vs 451-525), i.e. no signal either way. The lengths (263 tokens vs 261 letters) and the opening code-like signs ('ħ y nō' for 'El conte Girolamo'?) keep the hypothesis alive. Needs a careful sign-by-sign transcription of c. 13r at higher resolution (the BNCF viewer serves 985 px only) and a proper homophonic crib attack; if it fits, verdict read (contemporary clear), if it is excluded, open.
prior_unvetted: Leaf seen, no gloss, but whether Lorenzo de' Medici, Lettere prints it is not settled. BNCF teca image BNCF0003827895 (c. 13r, 985x217, downloaded and enlarged 6 Nov 2026): a 40x209 mm strip, four full lines of symbol cipher, roughly 300 signs, with no sender, date, address or interlinear gloss; c. 13v holds only show-through and the BNCF stamp (inv. 3423197). Manus 611145 gives no sender, date or Lettere reference for it, though it cites Lettere for cc. 6-9 (VI p. 26) and cc. 20-21 (V p. 260). Google Books feed probes show the Censimento (1964) lists many Lorenzo pieces in 'BNF, GC, 137' with editor-assigned addressees and dates ('[Niccolo Michelozzi ?]' [giu. 1484 ?], [giu.] 1488, [dic. 1489]), and Lettere volumes cite GC 137 cc. 6-9, 20-21, 22-23/26/35, 34, 52-53; c. 13 was not found in the snippets, but the biglietto could be one of the bracketed Censimento items and printed, deciphered or not, in Lettere. Needs Chrome: https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/seEYGFQqM1kC?gbpv=1&bsq=GC,%20137 (Censimento) and the same bsq 'GC, 137, c. 13' in Lettere vols. Chrome pass c32 with the old Google Books interface (books.google.fr/books?id=FjzUAAAAMAAJ&newbks=0&q=...): p. 290 snippet shows the heading 'Kővár, 1678 október 10. Teleki Mihály Rhédey Ferencznek' and 'irott Kgld levelét¹ böcsülettel vöttem ...' in clear; a sweep of 'Ferencznek N' for N = 10-99 hits p. 290 only for 10 (the date) and 73, so p. 290 carries no printed number groups; the cipher Lang describes ('számok, valószínűleg homof., megfejtetlen', Lang 2015 p. 292; p. 68 n. 87: the whole ciphered part unresolved) must be on pp. 291-292, which no anchor word reached. The edition's convention is now proven on p. 307 (no. 283, Rhédey's reply): unresolved numbers in brackets '[140 131 124 123]¹' and the deciphered word in italics ('leggonoszabbak'), so no. 266's numbers are very likely printed bare. Same volume p. 88 holds a page dense with numbers (hits for 12-88 with 'Ferencznek'), another cipher letter, not this lead. Needs Teleki VIII pp. 291-292 (HathiTrust with the Cloudflare check cleared by the user, or a library copy).
